title: Dressmaker review – delightful business sim is a cut above
summary: PC; Cosy Lives/Free Lives Catering to the exacting whims of a small town preparing for some grand visitors presents absorbing, beautifully designed – and surprisingly thrilling – challenges The small town of Twillford is abuzz with intrigue and excitement. A local duke has died and ladies of a certain standing are determined to make an impression at the funeral. As a newly arrived dressmaker with the only clothing shop in the area, you’re about to get plenty of work. Thus begins this utterly delightful sim game, in which you talk to customers, gather their style preferences and tailor specific outfits just for them. It could be a suitably respectful funeral frock, with just a hint of style to catch the eye of the duke’s wealthy relatives, or perhaps a work outfit for a farmer who loves bright colours. Once you have your brief, you open your sketchbook and draft a pattern using fabric swatches and a pencil to colour in your design. Need something elegant? How about a strapless bodice. An outfit for the office? A pencil skirt is a good call. Continue reading...

title: Dozens of court cases in England and Wales affected by undisclosed AI use in 2026
summary: Exclusive: Investigation finds at least 25 cases affected by AI-generated witness statements, fictitious case law and nonexistent statutes Undisclosed AI use has affected more than two dozen court cases this year, prompting judges to complain about AI-generated witness statements, fictitious case law and nonexistent statutes, an investigation has revealed. Proceedings where judges have been forced to deal with lawyers, police officers and claimants misusing the technology in 2026 include a high court dispute between tax lawyers marred by what the judge called “unacceptable” use of “generative AI hallucinations” and references to nonexistent cases. title: Elon Musk pledges to give two SpaceX shares to every child in the US
summary: The total value of the shares could reach almost $18bn and comes as tech companies debate how to share the spoils of the AI boom Elon Musk, the world’s richest person, has pledged to give every child in the US two shares in SpaceX, the space ⁠and AI company he ​runs, worth a total of almost $18bn. In a brief post on X, the social media platform that he owns, Musk said children will receive one share from the company itself, and one from him personally. SpaceX announced earlier on Wednesday that it would ​contribute one newly issued share of its Class A common stock ‌to every currently active Trump Account, and that ‌Musk will match the number of shares it donates. title: Slow internet? The best wifi extenders and mesh systems to boost your home network – tested
summary: We put 11 range extenders and mesh systems to the test to find the fastest and most reliable for streaming, gaming and working from home • The best office chairs Fast fibre broadband is fantastic – if the wifi signal reaches the part of your home where you need it. Most of us use the router provided by our broadband provider, often tucked away in a hallway or corner of the lounge. Sadly, these often don’t have the range to cover every room in your home, leaving you high and dry when you’re trying to binge-watch TV or get work done in a distant home office. Wifi extenders and mesh systems can help. Extenders plug in to a mains socket between your location and the router, then pass data backwards and forwards to extend your router’s reach. Mesh systems are even smarter, pairing a secondary router with one or two satellite units, which work together to extend the wifi coverage throughout your home. The mesh system can pass your connection from unit to unit to make sure you’re always getting the best possible link from your device to the internet, wherever you are in your home.
